plan_evidence.strategy: Trim the last removable interpreter work from the hot path: pre-bind the current-stream getter at import and use a bare subscript lookup with exception-based compile-on-miss.
plan_evidence.code_changes: Resolved the current-stream getter once at import into _GET_STREAM (probe: raw(0) accepted, else a no-arg/torch.npu fallback) so run() makes one call with no intermediate Python frame; replaced the _ENTRIES.get(...) + None branch with a subscript lookup inside try/except KeyError; kept the numel early return, the contiguity/shape guards, the alignment gate, the cached launch tuple and the 8192 tile cap unchanged.
plan_evidence.hypothesis: The measured per-call budget on 1024-element fp16 is 9.0-9.2 us for the raw launcher, ~1.4 us for the contiguity/shape/pointer guards, ~0.8 us for the dtype/numel dict key and lookup, ~0.34 us for the stream query and the rest interpreter frame work, giving 13.4-14.6 us for run() overall. The guards and the launch cannot be removed, so only the stream indirection and the lookup form are available; a nested Python call was measured at ~1.5 us, so eliminating one frame should be visible.

expected_effect.mechanism: Removing one Python call frame (_stream) and one LOAD_METHOD/CALL pair (dict.get) from every invocation trims a fixed fraction of a microsecond from the per-call cost, which shifts all nine launch-overhead-dominated workloads by roughly the same amount.
